items.title: Tell HN: VSCode/Cursor Exploit Actively Used by Scammers
items.body: I encountered this one personally - I was contacted on LinkedIn by someone interested in taking me on as a technical consultant. I agreed to meet with them. At the meeting, they asked me to clone their product's (public?!) repo and open it in Cursor or VSCode. I was immediately suspicious and refused. They disconnected and vanished from LinkedIn. I took a look over the repo (without touching, of course) and spotted the exploit - VSCode will happily auto-run tasks listed in `tasks.json`. In this case, a task ran that harvested credentials from `process.env`, sent them to a remote server and then executed further code that the server sent back. items.title: Tell HN: OVH price increase for dedicated servers
items.body: Since October 1 the OVH price increase also applies to running dedicated servers, at next renewal. A Reddit user posted that their two servers went up 54% in 11 months, no grandfathering. OVH's own post: an Advance-1 Gen 2024 renews at $114.99 instead of $89.99 (+28%). RAM options on new orders are up 68% to 652%, the Game range up to 87%. The stated reason is DDR5 costing six times what it did a year ago. Hetzner did the same in February and June, both threads had 500+ points here. I run a small PHP hosting company, so I am biased. But I wonder: Who here still runs OVH or Hetzner dedicated boxes? Sources: https://blog.ovhcloud.com/en/posts/dedicated-servers-pricing-update-h2-2026/ https://itdaily.com/news/cloud/ovhcloud-price-increase-ram/ https://www.reddit.com/r/webhosting/comments/1wvf

items.title: The 10-Product-a-Day API Limit That Changed How I Ship Digital Products
items.body:
I built an uploader that could create a hundred products in an afternoon. Then it started failing after ten. 

 No error message worth reading. No rate-limit header. Just ten successes and then nothing, every time I tried a batch. 

 That day I learned a rule that is not in any tutorial: some platforms cap how much you can  create , not how fast you can call the API. It is an anti-spam limit, and it resets on a rolling 24-hour clock. 

 
  
  
  Why the cap exists, and why it is fine
 

 Once I stopped being annoyed, the logic was obvious. A store that lets one account dump a thousand listings overnight is a spam farm. A rolling daily cap keeps the marketplace usable.

items.title: I Ran a Whole Content Pipeline on a $7 VPS With 2GB of RAM (And the 3am Crash That Taught Me Why)
items.body:
The cron job ran at 3am. By 3:02 the server was unreachable. 

 Not slow. Gone. SSH timing out, no response, nothing in the logs because the thing that writes the logs had itself been killed. 

 The cause was not a bug. It was arithmetic. A batch job that looked harmless on my laptop quietly needed more memory than the box had, and the kernel did what kernels do: it picked a victim and killed it. 

 
  
  
  Why cheap servers fail differently
 

 On a big machine, memory pressure is a performance problem. On a 2GB box, it is an availability problem. You do not get "slow". You get "dead", and you get it at the worst possible time, which is always 3am.

items.title: A Gumroad Store With 39 Products and No Visitors (What I Got Wrong About Distribution)
items.body:
I built 39 products and got almost no sales. For a while I thought the products were bad. 

 They were not. The problem was simpler and more embarrassing: I had built a cash register and expected it to bring customers. 

 
  
  
  The mistake, stated plainly
 

 A marketplace like Gumroad does three things well. It takes payment, it delivers files, and it handles tax. It does not send you buyers. Listing on a marketplace is like opening a shop in a town with no roads leading to it. 

 I had confused  being available for sale  with  being found . Those are two different jobs, and only one of them was done.

items.title: How I Turn AI Images Into Print-Ready Vector Stickers (No Illustrator, No GPU)
items.body:
AI image tools are great at exactly one thing: making a picture that looks right at 1024 pixels. 

 Marketplaces and crafters need something else. They need a file that stays sharp at any size, opens in Cricut Design Space, and can be recoloured by a buyer who has never opened Illustrator. A PNG is a photograph of a sticker. An SVG is the sticker. 

 For a while I was selling the wrong one. 

 
  
  
  The gap nobody mentions
 

 When you prompt an AI image model, you get raster art. Pixels in a grid. Zoom in and the edges turn into a staircase. Upload it to a stock site and it gets rejected as "not vector". Hand it to a Cricut user and the cut line comes out fuzzy.

items.title: I Made 39 Digital Products and Sold Almost Nothing. The Product Was Never the Problem.
items.body:
I still remember refreshing the dashboard at 2am, hoping the number would change. 

 It did not. Thirty-nine products in the store, a clean landing page, decent covers, and almost no sales. I had done the thing every guide tells you to do. Make a good product. Make more of them. Ship. 

 The problem was that I had optimised the wrong half of the business. 

 
  
  
  The trap of building
 

 Building feels like progress. You can see it. You generate the files, you write the description, you hit publish, and something new exists in the world that did not exist an hour ago. It is deeply satisfying, and that satisfaction hides a very simple fact. 

 A product nobody can find is a product nobody can buy.

items.title: How I Run a Full Content Pipeline on a $7 VPS With 2GB of RAM (And the 3am Crash That Taught Me Why)
items.body:
The cron job ran at 3am and the server went dark. 

 I woke up to a dead SSH session, a swap file that had been chewed through, and a pipeline that had produced nothing. The task was simple on paper: generate a batch of images, vectorise them, package them, upload them. On my laptop it took a few minutes. On a 1 vCPU box with 2GB of RAM it killed the machine. 

 I had written code that worked. I had not written code that fit. 

 
  
  
  Why small servers die
 

 The mistake was concurrency. I processed everything at once, because that is the default when you write a loop. Ten images in flight means ten copies of the model, ten decoded bitmaps, ten sets of intermediate buffers. On a big machine that is a rounding error.
